svg.title: ELEMENT DISCOVERY & PERIODIC-TABLE ORGANIZATION
svg.desc: fieldnotes educational infographic. Editable vector text and decorative scientific illustrations.

g.text: Element discovery transformed chemistry: from identifying substances in minerals and gases to detecting atoms made in laboratories.
Carl Wilhelm Scheele · Uppsala, Sweden · Scheele’s laboratory and
Scheele produced greenish-yellow chlorine by heating hydrochloric acid with
pyrolusite. Humphry Davy later proved it was an element (1810).
Bernard Courtois · Paris, France · Courtois’s saltpetre works and
Courtois saw violet vapour while processing seaweed ash. Gay-Lussac later named
the element after its violet colour.
Antoine-Jérôme Balard · Montpellier, France · University of
Balard identified an orange-red liquid in brine residues. Carl Löwig had
solar-spectroscopy observations; Janssen at Guntur and Lockyer in
Janssen and Lockyer independently detected a new yellow line in the Sun’s
spectrum. Helium was isolated on Earth in 1895.
Jean Charles Galissard de Marignac · Geneva, Switzerland · University
De Marignac separated a new oxide from erbium. The material still contained
Henri Moissan · Paris, France · École supérieure de pharmacie de Paris
Moissan isolated F₂ by electrolysing potassium bifluoride in liquid hydrogen
fluoride after decades of dangerous failed attempts.
Dale R. Corson, Kenneth R. MacKenzie & Emilio Segrè · Berkeley, USA ·
University of California, Berkeley Radiation Laboratory
Bombarding bismuth with alpha particles produced this extremely radioactive
element. Only tiny quantities can be made.
Albert Ghiorso, Glenn Seaborg & Berkeley team · Berkeley, USA ·
University of California Radiation Laboratory; 60-inch cyclotron
Seventeen atoms were made by bombarding einsteinium-253 with alpha particles.
Joint Institute for Nuclear Research team · Dubna, USSR · Joint
After disputed 1957–58 claims, Dubna achieved a conclusive synthesis in 1965.
The early Swedish claim was later shown to be incorrect.
JINR Dubna · Lawrence Livermore · Oak Ridge collaboration · JINR U-400
cyclotron; Oak Ridge and Lawrence Livermore national laboratories
Calcium-48 ions were fused with berkelium-249. IUPAC confirmed the discovery in
Discovery advanced from chemical isolation and solar spectroscopy to accelerator-made nuclei through international collaboration.
Sources: Royal Society of Chemistry element histories · ACS Transuranium Elements at Berkeley Lab · IUPAC discovery and naming reports.
